tool_input.command:
git add internal/mission/aborted_writer_drift_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
docs+test(mission): fix the drift guard's stated criterion, add ReturnStmt (A, F)

Review finding A (full-branch review, m-2026-09-08-004 round 3),
HIGHEST PRIORITY: the drift guard's own doc comment said the three
DelegationVerdictAborted write sites "all fire BEFORE a worker process
starts" -- three lines above its own wantSites list, which names
store.go's Close sweep as one of the three. That site stamps aborted on
delegations whose worker DID run; the comment contradicted its own
test. The actual invariant, already correctly stated in
countBlockingDelegations's own doc comment: every writer is unreachable
from the gate while its mission is still open, not "before the worker
starts." Rewrote the guard's comment to state the real reachability
argument (Close's sweep can fire against a delegation whose worker ran,
but only once the mission is already non-open -- one precondition short
of Abandon's own StatusOpen gate) so a future reviewer re-justifies a
fourth writer against the criterion that actually matters, not a
simpler one that would wave through the exact case that breaks the
exclusion.

Review finding F (full-branch review, m-2026-09-08-004 round 3), LOW:
*ast.ReturnStmt was not a write position, so a helper like `func
abortVerdict() string { return DelegationVerdictAborted }` was
invisible to the scan, and its own callers registered only as an
ordinary CallExpr naming the helper -- never as a
DelegationVerdictAborted occurrence at all. Added *ast.ReturnStmt to
the write-position set. Falsified by inserting exactly that shape
(reverted after confirming the guard now catches it).
EOF
)"
